coverage_axes.notes: Independent learner and general dictionaries cover the principal noun, verb, military, crime, and operational uses.
Countability, noun complements, transitive frames, passive military frames, and operational idioms are represented.
Commissioner, decommission, recommission, and commission-free are represented as atomic forms; regular inflections are covered by the headword verb sources.
Military appointment, formal crime language, naval service, and engineering commissioning are directly covered.
Learner dictionaries identify formal, public, commercial, artistic, and crime-domain uses and their countability.
Oxford supplies pronunciation and Etymonline supplies the French and Latin history and semantic development.

facts.statement: A countable commission can be an official group responsible for control or investigation.
facts.source_detail: Oxford noun sense 1 gives an official group with responsibility to control or investigate.

facts.statement: Commission can be money paid for selling goods, commonly linked to the amount sold.
facts.source_detail: Oxford noun sense 2 supplies percentage and on-commission examples.

facts.statement: Commission can be a charge made by a bank or similar provider for a service.
facts.source_detail: Oxford noun sense 3 distinguishes the charge from salesperson remuneration.

facts.statement: A commission can be a formal request to design or make a work, with to, for, and from complements.
facts.source_detail: Oxford noun sense 4 gives commission to do, commission for, and commission from patterns.

facts.statement: In armed forces usage, a commission is an officer's position and authority.
facts.source_detail: Oxford noun sense 5 identifies the officer position and contrasts commissioned officer.

facts.statement: In formal usage, the commission of a crime means the act of doing the crime.
facts.source_detail: Oxford labels this crime sense uncountable and formal.

facts.statement: In or out of commission expresses whether something is available for use.
facts.source_detail: Oxford's idiom entry gives temporarily out-of-commission aircraft.

facts.statement: The noun and verb are pronounced /kəˈmɪʃən/ in British and American English.
facts.source_detail: Oxford noun and verb entries give matching British and American pronunciations and regular verb forms.

facts.statement: Commission can denote formal authority, a formal request for paid work, or the work so produced.
facts.source_detail: Merriam-Webster separates a warrant or authorization, a paid creative request, and a commissioned work.

facts.statement: Commission can denote an official group directed to perform a duty.
facts.source_detail: Merriam-Webster gives both a duty-specific group and government agency uses.

facts.statement: Commission is a fee paid to an agent or employee for a transaction or service, especially a percentage.
facts.source_detail: Merriam-Webster defines the commercial payment and illustrates commission per sale.

facts.statement: Commission can be the act of committing or doing something, especially wrongdoing.
facts.source_detail: Merriam-Webster illustrates the act-of-committing sense with commission of a crime.

facts.statement: The transitive verb can formally engage a person to do work or order a work to be made.
facts.source_detail: Merriam-Webster verb examples include being commissioned to write and commissioning a portrait.

facts.statement: The verb can appoint a military officer and can put a ship into active service.
facts.source_detail: Merriam-Webster lists officer appointment and ship activation as verb uses.

facts.statement: Commissioner denotes a person entrusted with commission duties or a member or head of a commission.
facts.source_detail: Merriam-Webster's related commissioner entry records the official role.

facts.statement: Commission-free describes a transaction for which no commission is directly charged.
facts.source_detail: Merriam-Webster's commission definition and common attributive commercial formation support the transparent compound.

facts.statement: The verb formally chooses or asks someone to do a special piece of work and can take a work as object.
facts.source_detail: Cambridge verb coverage distinguishes requesting work and appointing an officer.

facts.statement: The noun covers an official group, payment for selling, commissioned work, and formal wrongdoing.
facts.source_detail: Cambridge groups these as separate noun senses with learner-level examples.

facts.statement: In commission means active service or usable condition; out of commission means inactive or unusable condition.
facts.source_detail: American Heritage distinguishes the naval sense and its general equipment extension and lists commissioning a ship.

facts.statement: Commission entered through Old French from Latin commissio and committere, built from com- and mittere, with delegated-authority senses preceding later commercial and naval uses.
facts.source_detail: Etymonline dates delegated authority, a duty-bearing body, commercial percentage, naval service, and later general out-of-commission extension.

facts.statement: Decommission is the reversive verb for removing something from active service.
facts.source_detail: Etymonline cross-references decommission as a productive derivative of commission.

facts.statement: Recommission means to commission again or return something to active service.
facts.source_detail: Etymonline cross-references recommission as the repeated-action derivative.

sources.title: Whole Building Design Guide — Building Commissioning

facts.statement: Building commissioning is a documented process of planning, installation, testing, verification, and transition to operations against owner requirements.
facts.source_detail: WBDG describes commissioning as a professional process spanning design through testing, documentation, and operation.

source_union.canonical_statement: Commission denotes an official duty-bearing group or public body.
Commission denotes transaction-linked remuneration paid to a salesperson or agent.
Commission can denote a transaction or service charge paid by a customer.
source_union.rationale: Learner-relevant role reversal from sales remuneration.

source_union.canonical_statement: A commission is a formal paid request for creative or professional work and can denote the resulting work.
Military commission denotes or grants officer rank and authority.
source_union.rationale: Distinct specialist noun and verb use.

source_union.canonical_statement: The commission of wrongdoing is the formal act of committing it.
In/out of commission marks active or usable versus inactive or unusable status.
The verb formally engages someone to perform work or orders work to be produced.
Technical commissioning verifies and transitions installed systems into documented operation.
source_union.rationale: Direct specialist support for the engineering use.

source_union.canonical_statement: Commission has common British-American pronunciation /kəˈmɪʃən/ and derives through French from Latin committere.
Commissioner is the person-form derived from commission.
Decommission reverses commission by removing from active service.
Recommission means to return to active service or commission again.
Commission-free means that no commission is directly charged.

claim_units.statement: Commission is an official group with a public or assigned duty.

source_supports.support_summary: Oxford directly defines the official group sense.
Merriam-Webster directly covers duty-bearing commissions.
Cambridge independently covers the official group sense.

claim_units.statement: Commercial commission is sales-linked remuneration to an agent or employee.

source_supports.support_summary: Oxford gives percentage and on-commission remuneration.
Merriam-Webster defines agent or employee transaction payment.
Cambridge independently covers payment for selling.

claim_units.statement: Commission can be a bank, broker, or service-provider transaction charge.

source_supports.support_summary: Oxford explicitly separates the customer charge sense.

claim_units.statement: A commission is a formal request or resulting work with to, for, and from complements.

source_supports.support_summary: Oxford supplies the noun complement frames.
Merriam-Webster covers both request and resulting work.

claim_units.statement: Military commission is officer appointment, rank, authority, or warrant and commission as a verb grants it.

source_supports.support_summary: Oxford defines the officer-position noun use.
Merriam-Webster covers officer appointment as a verb.

claim_units.statement: The commission of wrongdoing is a formal legal nominalization of committing it.

source_supports.support_summary: Oxford labels the crime construction formal and uncountable.
Merriam-Webster defines commission as an act of committing.
Cambridge independently lists the crime sense.

claim_units.statement: The idiom contrasts active or usable status with inactive or unusable status.

source_supports.support_summary: Oxford directly defines the availability contrast.
American Heritage covers naval and general operational status.
Etymonline documents the naval origin and later extension.

claim_units.statement: The transitive verb formally requests a person to work or orders a work.

source_supports.support_summary: Merriam-Webster gives person and work-object examples.
Cambridge independently covers the formal request verb.

claim_units.statement: Engineering commissioning includes verification, documentation, and transition to operation.

source_supports.support_summary: WBDG directly describes the technical commissioning process.

claim_units.statement: Commission is pronounced /kəˈmɪʃən/ and derives through French from Latin committere.

source_supports.support_summary: Oxford supplies matching British-American pronunciation.
Etymonline traces the French and Latin history.

claim_units.statement: Commissioner denotes a member or official entrusted with commission duties.

source_supports.support_summary: Merriam-Webster records the official person derivative.

claim_units.statement: Decommission removes a ship, system, or facility from active service.

source_supports.support_summary: Etymonline records the reversive derivative.

claim_units.statement: Recommission returns something to active service or commissions it again.

source_supports.support_summary: Etymonline records the repeated-action derivative.

claim_units.statement: Commission-free marks a transaction without a directly charged commission.

source_supports.support_summary: Merriam-Webster's commercial sense supports the transparent compound.
